ocean_surface_settlements.weatherLife: Salt haze, squalls, moon-tide fog, floating docks.
ocean_surface_settlements.settlementResponse: Tide stairs, breakaway piers, shell gardens, roof nets, fog horns.

reef_shallows.weatherLife: Clear warm water, reef glare, spawning tides, storm surge.
reef_shallows.settlementResponse: Reef law, current pilots, coral masonry, moonlit closures.

deep_water_without_reefs.weatherLife: Cold upwelling, pressure roads, trench fog.
deep_water_without_reefs.settlementResponse: Submarine locks, pressure shrines, bioluminescent charts, brine taboos.

farming_plains.weatherLife: Warm field winds, flood canals, mildew seasons.
farming_plains.settlementResponse: Raised granaries, smokehouses, reed filters, moon-timed planting.

grassland_and_prairie.weatherLife: Dryline storms, fire season, herd weather.
grassland_and_prairie.settlementResponse: Mobile herds, burn laws, cistern stones, storm cellars.

mountain_range.weatherLife: Rain-making slopes, ridge lightning, rare high ice.
mountain_range.settlementResponse: Terraces, landslide walls, sky bridges, lightning towers.

valleys.weatherLife: Fog bowls, fruit belts, river crossings.
valleys.settlementResponse: Drainage ditches, fog bells, orchard shrines, fever marsh patrols.

deep_cavern.weatherLife: Stable damp air, mineral rivers, fungal lamps.
deep_cavern.settlementResponse: Vent shafts, cave flood alarms, fungus farms, stone reservoirs.

deep_forest.weatherLife: Canopy thunder, root roads, rot heat.
deep_forest.settlementResponse: Elevated paths, smoked stores, resin firebreaks, fungal guilds.

marsh_and_swamp.weatherLife: Blackwater, fever fog, mosquitoes, floating soil.
marsh_and_swamp.settlementResponse: Pole houses, reed boats, disease rites, amphibious markets.

polar_forest.weatherLife: Long light, long dark, wet gales, thin harbor skim.
polar_forest.settlementResponse: Light halls, food vaults, tide clocks, communal winter law.

hybrid_coastlands.weatherLife: Beach, reef, grass, farm, and forest in close reach.
hybrid_coastlands.settlementResponse: Mixed travel law: ferry, caravan, skyship, and canal authority overlap.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Copper-Silver King Tide
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: When both moons favor the sea at once, harbor stones vanish and reef roads drown.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Hushed Neap
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A low, quiet tide that exposes mud gates, wreck bones, and hidden causeways.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Storm-Stack Tide
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A low-pressure sea storm arriving with a strong moon tide.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Bastveig Drawdown
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A sudden retreat of water before trench-fed surge returns.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Horundar Wall
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A black-green wall of rain that crosses whole coasts.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Nannara Bead Squalls
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Short, sharp squalls that arrive in pairs or trios every few days.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Seleneš Silver Fog
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Moonlit fog so bright it makes ships look closer than they are.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Dragon-Anvil Cloud
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A towering thunderhead that forms over heated highlands.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Hag-Lantern Mist
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Greenish swamp fog carrying spores, firefly light, and bad directions.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Cockatrice Still
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A suffocating, windless heat that freezes sails and tempers alike.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Beholder’s Eye Cyclone
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A rotating storm whose calm center is ringed by clear, staring sky.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Goblin Drum Thunder
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Low rolling thunder that repeats long before the rain reaches a settlement.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Kobold Sump Breath
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Warm gas-fog from marsh canals and low cave mouths.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Spiderweb Rain
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A fine crosswind rain that seems to fall sideways from many directions.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Basilisk Glass Haze
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Shimmering heat that turns distance into false water and false stone.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Chimera Crosswind
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Three winds meeting over cliffs, reefs, or a canyon mouth.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Kraken-Surge
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A steep, dark swell pushed by far-off pressure changes.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Trollwash Rot-Rain
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Warm rain that wakes rot, swollen roots, and hungry fungus.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Owlbear Dusk Gust
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A sudden evening wind that turns forest travel loud and blind.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Manticore Dusthook
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A hooked dust plume ahead of dryline storms.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Wyvern Ridge Lightning
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Highland lightning that walks along exposed ridges.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Gelatinous Roadmire
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Rain-soaked clay roads that swallow carts and boots.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Mimic Puddle Season
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A season when road puddles hide sinkholes, leeches, and false bottoms.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Ghoulwind
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A dry graveyard wind that carries dust, spores, and old sickness.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Griffon Updraft
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A clean mountain lift used by skyships and great birds.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Sahuagin Undertow
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A fast pull beneath reef water during strong tide shifts.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Banshee Rain
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: Thin cold rain that whistles through ruins and empty rigging.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Hydra Floodpulse
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: One storm-fed river splits into several dangerous surges.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Wyrmcoil Current
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A spiraling river or sea current that turns boats sideways.

namedWeatherGlossary.name: Moonmoth Bloom
namedWeatherGlossary.meaning: A soft glowing insect and spore bloom after warm moon rain.

canonicalRevision.spatialAuthority: Final 2048 x 1024 equirectangular anchors and province transforms from the corrected geological/weather compendium override every earlier coordinate, UTC, mapped-biome/depth, and route geometry value.
canonicalRevision.nonSpatialAuthority: Current pantheon/races and life compendia preserve and extend non-spatial canon; the newest night-sky/time compendium governs calendar, celestial, and exact settlement UTC data.
